episodes.198859: A powerful storm system moving through the Upper Great Lakes generated storm force west winds across much of Lake Superior on the 27th.
episodes.199323: The dry weather pattern with 7 Santa Ana wind events in January finally broke and gave way to a cold Pacific storm in late January.  This produced widespread precipitation and heavy snowfall in the mountains. There was 6 to 16 inches of new snow in the San Bernardino mountains above 5000 feet. 3 to 6 inches of snow occurred in the San Jacinto mountains January 26-27 and up to 10 inches in Palomar mountain.
